browse.usage.hint.mavenDependency: Add it to the dependencies of your pom.xml
browse.usage.hint.gradleKotlinPublish: Add it to build.gradle.kts next to the maven-publish plugin; Gradle reads the user and password from the astrumUsername and astrumPassword properties
browse.usage.hint.gradleGroovyPublish: Add it to build.gradle next to the maven-publish plugin; Gradle reads the user and password from the astrumUsername and astrumPassword properties
browse.usage.hint.mavenSettingsHosted: Save it as ~/.m2/settings.xml to use the repository in every build
browse.usage.hint.mavenSettingsMirror: Save it as ~/.m2/settings.xml to get every dependency through this repository
browse.usage.hint.mavenDeploy: Add it to pom.xml and run mvn deploy; put the credentials in a server with the same id in settings.xml
browse.usage.hint.npmrc: Save it in the .npmrc of the project or of your home directory
browse.usage.hint.npmrcScoped: Save it in .npmrc: packages of this scope come from here, all others from your usual registry
browse.usage.hint.npmPublish: Sign in once, then publish from the package folder
browse.usage.hint.npmLogin: Sign in once when the repository does not allow anonymous reading
browse.usage.hint.nugetSource: Register the repository once as a package source
browse.usage.hint.nugetConfig: Put into NuGet.Config next to the solution
browse.usage.hint.nugetPush: The API key is the NuGet API key of your user on this server
browse.usage.hint.twine: twine asks for the user name and password of this server
browse.usage.hint.dockerLogin: Sign in once before pulling from or pushing to this registry
browse.usage.hint.dockerfile: Use the image as the base of your own
browse.usage.hint.dockerPush: Tag your local image with this address, then push it
browse.usage.hint.rawSignIn: Add -u <user> when the repository needs a sign-in
browse.usage.hint.rawUpload: Uploading needs a user who may add to this repository
browse.usage.hint.helmRepo: Register the repository once, then install charts from it
browse.usage.hint.helmUpload: Uploading needs a user with write access to this repository
browse.usage.hint.swiftDependency: Add to the dependencies in Package.swift, then run swift package resolve
browse.usage.hint.swiftLogin: Sign in once with your user of this server; Swift asks for the password
browse.usage.hint.swiftNetrc: Swift signs in over HTTPS only, so for plain HTTP put the user into ~/.netrc
browse.usage.hint.swiftPublish: Run in the package directory; the release metadata comes from package-metadata.json
browse.usage.hint.swiftRegistry: Run once in the package directory; add --global to use the registry for every package
browse.usage.hint.swiftRegistryHttp: Swift talks to a plain HTTP registry only with --allow-insecure-http; add --global to use the registry for every package
browse.usage.hint.hfDownload: Downloads into the Hugging Face cache; without a file name the whole repository
browse.usage.hint.hfEndpoint: Set once: huggingface_hub, transformers and the hf command then download through this repository. The longer timeout leaves time for large files the repository fetches for the first time. When the repository needs a sign-in, put user:token@ before the host name
browse.usage.hint.hfTransformers: With HF_ENDPOINT set, transformers loads the model through this repository
browse.usage.hint.terraformCredentials: Add to ~/.terraformrc; the first line fetches a token for your user once
browse.usage.hint.terraformMirror: Add to ~/.terraformrc to install every provider through this repository
browse.usage.hint.terraformProviderProxy: Add to a .tf file and install providers through this repository as a network mirror
browse.usage.hint.terraformRegistry: Add to a .tf file. Terraform looks the registry up at https://{host}/.well-known/terraform.json, so {host} must be the registry host of this repository or of a group it belongs to
browse.usage.hint.terraformUpload: Uploading needs a user with write access to this repository
browse.usage.hint.yumRepo: Save it as /etc/yum.repos.d/{name}.repo and install packages with dnf or yum
browse.usage.hint.yumUpload: Uploading needs a user with write access to this repository
browse.usage.hint.gemfile: Put this at the top of the project's Gemfile
browse.usage.hint.bundleMirror: Run it once; Bundler then fetches every gem from rubygems.org through this repository
browse.usage.hint.gemSources: Add the repository once as a source of the gem command
browse.usage.hint.gemPush: RUBYGEMS_HOST sends gem signin, push and yank to this repository; sign in once as a user of this server to get an API key
browse.usage.hint.lfsConfig: Run it in the git repository and commit .lfsconfig, so that every clone keeps its large files here
browse.usage.hint.lfsLocalConfig: Run it in a clone to keep its large files in this repository without committing anything
browse.usage.hint.lfsObject: Downloads the object by its SHA-256, as git lfs does when it checks out a file
browse.usage.hint.cargoConfig: Put into .cargo/config.toml of the project or of your home directory
browse.usage.hint.cargoPublish: Sign in once with a token of this server, then publish from the crate directory
browse.usage.hint.goEnv: Set once; go commands then fetch modules through this repository
browse.usage.hint.goEnvPrivate: Set once; the module is not in the public checksum database, so it is not checked there
browse.usage.hint.goUpload: Uploading needs a user with write access to this repository
browse.usage.hint.aptSources: Put into /etc/apt/sources.list.d/{name}.list and import the signing key of the repository
browse.usage.hint.aptUpload: Uploading needs a user with write access to this repository
browse.usage.hint.composerConfig: Run once in the project to add the repository to composer.json
browse.usage.hint.composerUpload: Uploading needs a user with write access to this repository
browse.usage.hint.conanRemote: Register the repository once as a Conan remote
browse.usage.hint.conanUpload: Uploading needs a user with write access to this repository
browse.usage.hint.cocoapodsPodfile: Put the source line at the top of the Podfile; CocoaPods then reads every pod through this repository instead of trunk
browse.usage.hint.cocoapodsRepo: Add the repository once to the local spec repositories for pod spec cat and pod repo update
browse.usage.hint.cocoapodsNetrc: CocoaPods and curl read the user from ~/.netrc when the repository does not allow anonymous reading
browse.usage.hint.condarc: Save it as ~/.condarc to install packages from this channel by default
browse.usage.hint.condaUpload: Uploading needs a user with write access to this repository
browse.usage.hint.rProfile: Put into ~/.Rprofile to install from this repository next to the repositories set before
browse.usage.hint.rProfileMirror: Put into ~/.Rprofile; R then installs every package through this repository instead of CRAN
browse.usage.hint.rDescription: Add the package to the Imports field of your package's DESCRIPTION
browse.usage.hint.rUpload: Uploading needs a user with write access to this repository
browse.usage.hint.pubToken: Run it once and paste an access token of your account when asked; dart pub sends it with every request to this repository
browse.usage.hint.pubDependency: Add the dependency to pubspec.yaml of your package, then run dart pub get
browse.usage.hint.pubPublish: Put into pubspec.yaml of your package, then run dart pub publish from its directory
browse.usage.hint.pubHostedUrl: dart pub then takes every package that names no other repository from here instead of pub.dev
browse.usage.hint.nixConfig: Put into /etc/nix/nix.conf (or extra-substituters in a flake's nixConfig) and restart the Nix daemon. List the public keys of whoever signed the store paths, for example cache.nixos.org-1:6NCHdD59X431o0gWypbMrAURkbJ16ZPMQFGspcDShjY= for a proxy of cache.nixos.org
browse.usage.hint.nixNetrc: Nix sends these credentials to the repository; leave the file out if anonymous users may read it. Create an access token on your account page
browse.usage.hint.nixPublish: Make a signing key once and give its public key to the clients in trusted-public-keys; nix copy signs the store paths and uploads them with the credentials of the netrc file
browse.usage.hint.p2Eclipse: Add the repository as a software site; Eclipse then installs and updates through it
browse.usage.hint.p2Tycho: Put into pom.xml of the Tycho build; it then resolves its target platform through this repository
browse.usage.hint.p2Director: Installs into the Eclipse that runs the command; add -destination to install into another one
browse.usage.hint.apkRepositories: Save the signing key once, then add the branch to /etc/apk/repositories
browse.usage.hint.apkUntrusted: The indexes of this repository are not signed, so apk needs --allow-untrusted
browse.usage.hint.apkUpload: Uploading needs a user with write access to this repository
browse.usage.hint.ansibleConfig: Put it into ansible.cfg next to your playbooks or into ~/.ansible.cfg; the token is an access token of this server and can be left out when the repository allows anonymous reading
browse.usage.hint.ansibleRequirements: Install everything the file lists with ansible-galaxy install -r requirements.yml
browse.usage.hint.ansiblePublish: Build the archive with ansible-galaxy collection build; publishing needs a user with write access to this repository
browse.usage.hint.chefBerksfile: Put it into the Berksfile and run berks install; Berkshelf reads the universe and the cookbooks without credentials, so let the anonymous user read this repository
browse.usage.hint.chefPolicyfile: Put it into Policyfile.rb and run chef install; Policyfiles also read this repository without credentials
browse.usage.hint.chefKnife: knife supermarket show, search and install take the same -m option
browse.usage.hint.chefPublish: knife supermarket share signs its requests with a Chef client key, which this server does not check, so publish with curl and a user with write access; the archive needs <name>/metadata.json, which knife cookbook metadata writes from metadata.rb
browse.usage.hint.puppetConfig: Put it into puppet.conf (puppet config print config shows where it is) for puppet module install; forge_authorization takes an access token of this server and can be left out when the repository allows anonymous reading
browse.usage.hint.puppetR10k: Put it into r10k.yaml; r10k then installs the Forge modules of your Puppetfiles from here
browse.usage.hint.puppetBolt: Put it into bolt-project.yaml or bolt-defaults.yaml; bolt module install then resolves and installs modules from here
browse.usage.hint.puppetfile: librarian-puppet reads the forge line; r10k keeps its own Forge setting unless allow_puppetfile_override is on
browse.usage.hint.puppetPublish: Run it in the module directory; publishing needs an access token of a user with write access to this repository
browse.usage.hint.puppetCurl: Sends an archive built with pdk build or puppet module build, as puppet-blacksmith does
browse.usage.hint.vagrantServer: Vagrant then looks up short box names here and sends the token to every address of this host; the token is an access token of this server and can be left out when the repository allows anonymous reading
browse.usage.hint.vagrantBoxUrl: box_url points Vagrant at the metadata of the box, so vagrant box outdated and vagrant box update look for new versions here
browse.usage.hint.vagrantUpload: The path names the version, provider and architecture of the box; the repository computes its SHA-256 checksum and adds it to the metadata of the box
browse.usage.hint.hexRepo: Fetch the public key of this repository once and add the repository to Mix under its own name; add --auth-key with an access token when the repository needs a sign-in
browse.usage.hint.hexDependency: Add it to deps in mix.exs; repo: names the repository added with mix hex.repo add
browse.usage.hint.hexRebar: Put it into rebar.config or ~/.config/rebar3/rebar.config with the contents of the downloaded public key; rebar3 then looks for packages in this repository before hex.pm
browse.usage.hint.hexPublish: Run it in the project directory with an access token of a user with write access to this repository; it publishes the package and its documentation
browse.usage.hint.hexMirror: Mix then fetches the packages of hex.pm through this repository and still checks their registry with the key of hex.pm
browse.usage.hint.hexCdn: rebar3 then fetches the packages of hex.pm through this repository
browse.usage.hint.openvsxProduct: Merge it into the product.json of VSCodium or another VS Code based editor, or into the product.json in its user data folder, and restart the editor; editors send no credentials, so the repository must allow anonymous reading
browse.usage.hint.openvsxEnvironment: Editors such as VSCodium also take the gallery from these variables; set them before starting the editor
browse.usage.hint.openvsxPublish: Package the extension with vsce package or let ovsx package it; the token is an access token of this server
